AMZN.rationale: Amazon's franchise is among the strongest in public markets — AWS reaccelerating to 28% YoY growth at a $150B run rate, advertising exceeding $70B trailing revenue at ~80% incremental margins, and a custom silicon business with a $225B Trainium backlog. Q1 2026 results showed record 13.1% operating margin and $30.3B net income, resolving the Q3 2025 operating-income dip that the quant report flagged. However, the stock is priced at 38.1x trailing PE — the top of its 365-day range (28.2–39.0) — with a 2.6% earnings yield against a 4.57% 10-year Treasury, creating a negative 197bps spread. The +27.8% quarterly rally has been a multiple-expansion story, not an earnings-improvement story. Trailing FCF collapsed 95% to $1.2B due to $200B capex guidance, and oil at $100+/bbl is a forward margin headwind for the logistics-heavy business. The franchise quality and Q1 2026 margin acceleration prevent a negative score, but the stretched valuation, rate headwinds, and FCF suppression from unprecedented capex spending limit upside from current levels. Near-term catalysts are limited — the next earnings event is the key test of whether the capex cycle is translating into margin expansion.
